comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

I can reproduce with built-in Lua tree-sitter parser. But this seems to happen only for `@parameter.outer`+`@parameter.inner` pair. Using 'nvim-treesitter' (current default) throws error while using built-in `vim.treesitter` just doesn't find a surrounding. I'll take a look.

---

As surrounding based on `@parameter.{outer,inner}` pair doesn't look useful to me (it usually matches a comma and some whitespace), what is your use case for this surrounding?

Actually, it seems I hadn't thought this completely through, you are right that it doesn't really make sense to use. I think I actually wanted the 'saaa{' ('[s]urround [a]dd [a]round [a]rgument [{]') actions, which works with just default 'mini.surround' + 'nvim-treesitter-context'. Should I close this issue or leave it open since it seems to be a bug, albeit quite inconsequential?

> Should I close this issue or leave it open since it seems to be a bug, albeit quite inconsequential?

I am pretty sure that it is either 'nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter' or `vim.treesitter` issue. Let's keep it open for a while, so that I'd not forget to try to take a closer look into it.

I'm actually getting the same error on Javascript files with the following config

```lua
    local surround = require "mini.surround"
    local ts_input = surround.gen_spec.input.treesitter
    surround.setup {
      custom_surroundings = {
        F = {
          input = ts_input { outer = "@call.outer", inner = "@call.inner" },
          output = function()
            local fun_name = surround.user_input "Function name"
            if fun_name == nil then return end
            return { left = ("%s("):format(fun_name), right = ")" }
          end,
        },
      },
    }
```

when trying to delete the surrounding function call in the code

```javascript
new Error("There are no credentials");
//                   ^--- The cursor is here
```

which uses [this](https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter-textobjects/blob/9937e5e356e5b227ec56d83d0a9d0a0f6bc9cad4/queries/ecma/textobjects.scm#L165-L176) capture from `nvim-treesitter-textobjects`

The problem happens because `mini.surround` uses `ts_queries.get_capture_matches_recursively(0, captures.outer, 'textobjects')`

https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/88f18a7d018d8bb4d32f6be4c712134a10e826d3/lua/mini/surround.lua#L1500

which returns the following when using a capture that relies on `#make-range!`

```
{ {
    node = { 0, 4, 0, 37,
      buf = 0,
      end_pos = { 0, 37, 37 },
      start_pos = { 0, 4, 4 },
      <metatable> = <1>{
        __index = <table 1>,
        child = <function 1>,
        child_count = <function 2>,
        collect_children = <function 3>,
        end_ = <function 4>,
        field = <function 5>,
        from_nodes = <function 6>,
        from_table = <function 7>,
        has_error = <function 8>,
        iter_children = <function 9>,
        missing = <function 10>,
        named = <function 11>,
        named_child = <function 12>,
        named_child_count = <function 13>,
        new = <function 14>,
        parent = <function 15>,
        range = <function 16>,
        sexpr = <function 17>,
        start = <function 18>,
        symbol = <function 19>,
        type = <function 20>
      }
    }
  }, {
    node = { 0, 4, 0, 37,
      buf = 0,
      end_pos = { 0, 37, 37 },
      start_pos = { 0, 4, 4 },
      <metatable> = <table 1>
    }
  } }
```

This fake nodes are then passed to `ts_queries.get_capture_matches` which in turns throws an errors because it's expecting a real node

https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/88f18a7d018d8bb4d32f6be4c712134a10e826d3/lua/mini/surround.lua#L1506

The fake nodes are coming from 

https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter/blob/835f5c11b8d4e1ded3576c69a019f717d3754c5a/lua/nvim-treesitter/query.lua#L278-L284

Thanks for details!

Yeah, indeed this seems like an issue with 'nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter' returning not the same data structures for `#make-range!` directives (which are present in `@parameter.outer` captures on `master` branch of 'nvim-treesitter').

I'll take a look if there is an easy-ish way to mitigate this in 'mini.surround' (and maybe 'mini.ai', as they share tree-sitter logic). If not, I'll open an 'nvim-treesitter' issue and call it a day.

A more important thing to notice here is that even using built-in `vim.treesitter` capabilities (i.e. [`use_nvim_treesitter = false`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/88f18a7d018d8bb4d32f6be4c712134a10e826d3/doc/mini-surround.txt#L836)) doesn't fully work with these `#make-range!` captures. This is because in that case `@parameter.outer` just is not recognized as a capture by `vim.treesitter.query.get('lang', 'textobjects').

Internally, `nvim-treesitter` only uses `get_capture_matches` on 

https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter/blob/835f5c11b8d4e1ded3576c69a019f717d3754c5a/lua/nvim-treesitter/query.lua#L445

where it always uses `tree:root()` as the node parameter of the function, (so there aren't any problems with using fake nodes).

Maybe an easy fix could be doing the same on `mini.surround`/`mini.ai`? I haven't looked into if it would work in 100% of the cases or there may be a performance penalty or edge case by doing so.

> A more important thing to notice here is that even using built-in vim.treesitter capabilities (i.e. [use_nvim_treesitter = false](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/88f18a7d018d8bb4d32f6be4c712134a10e826d3/doc/mini-surround.txt#L836)) doesn't fully work with these #make-range! captures. This is because in that case @parameter.outer just is not recognized as a capture by `vim.treesitter.query.get('lang', 'textobjects').

Yes, exactly. I didn't fully understand you earlier in matrix, sorry for that. As you said, those aren't really treesitter captures, `nvim-treesitter` just tries to use them as if they were.

In the end, I think there is no good/robust way of adjusting for the case of 'nvim-treesitter' returning not `TSNode` for such cases of custom directives. I *think* the motivation might be the same as I encountered here: no good/robust/exported way of actually creating a `TSNode` from scratch.

So I decided to at least account for such behavior by filtering out matches that don't contain node of actual `TSNode` type. This will make both `use_nvim_treesitter = true` and `use_nvim_treesitter = false` cases behave the same in this case and just show "No surrounding ... found".

There is also a [new note](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/0429e9ee9d35faef51971abdbb1b26d2540b5a5f/doc/mini-surround.txt#L824-L828) about this issue. It addresses only `vim.treesitter` as I do plan to eventually (maybe sooner rather than later) soft deprecate using 'nvim-treesitter' here in favor of only relying on built-in `vim.treesitter`. This might be after 'nvim-treesitter' switches to `main` branch permanently (which shouldn't have custom ways of doing things instead relying on `vim.treesitter` itself; no `#make-range!` either as can be seen in nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter-textobjects#612 which is tied to `main` branch of 'nvim-treesitter') or during this 'mini.nvim' release (starting with making `use_nvim_treesitter = false` the default).

---

@TheLeoP, thanks for looking into tree-sitter related things! I usually feel lost working with tree-sitter as it is somewhat overcomplicated with many abstractions that are not very clear to me.

That last note you linked from `mini.surround` is very important to `mini.ai` too. Custom textobjects such as `a = require("mini.ai").gen_spec.treesitter({ a = "@parameter.outer", i = "@parameter.inner" }),` are broken when using `master` treesitter-textobjects (the default).

What's the recommended way in order to keep everything working? There's currently no way to use `mini` modules without taking care to have `use_nvim_treesitter=true` everywhere, until one upgrades to `main` treesitter? Is there a more global overwrite?

I use `treesitter(-textobjects)?` just for the queries and I tried using `main` for both, but above custom textobject is not working correctly then either 🤔 Could be that `main` is just not ready for general use yet.

> That last note you linked from `mini.surround` is very important to `mini.ai` too. Custom textobjects such as `a = require("mini.ai").gen_spec.treesitter({ a = "@parameter.outer", i = "@parameter.inner" }),` are broken when using `master` treesitter-textobjects (the default).

The note is [also present in 'mini.ai' help](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/c3d398d8bfbd18ae24cb22a17cde1aaad3764cd3/doc/mini-ai.txt#L753-L757). I am not sure I'd say the `@parameter` is broken on `master`, but `aa` textobject indeed won't be found (because it uses documented unsupported directives on `master`).

There are indeed several solutions here:
- Use `main` branch of 'nvim-treesitter-textobjects'. This *kind of* works with the `main` 'mini.nvim' / 'mini.ai' branch: `aa` textobject will not include delimiter as it is marked as a separate match for `parameter.outer`.
- Use custom queries.
- Use built-in "argument" textobject, which doesn't rely on tree-sitter and should work in at least 95% of cases.

Oh, not sure how I missed it 🙏🏻

1. Yeah that's what I mean by "not working correctly" 😅 Would you say that's an error in the query?
2. I'm doing that for my main language (Go), but I have the `textobjects` installed for sane OOB captures. I can get the desired OOB experience by peppering the mini configs with the `use_nvim_treesitter` where required.
3. That's just sidestepping the problem though. Suppose I had asked after `function.inner` instead...

>     1. Yeah that's what I mean by "not working correctly" 😅 Would you say that's an error in the query?

I can't say if it is an error or not, because I think the main goal was to remove special directives from the `master` branch and current result is the best compromise. I think if somebody would try to fix this, the maintainers of 'nvim-treesitter' / 'nvim-treesitter-textobjects' will gladly help with advice.

>     2. I'm doing that for my main language (Go), but I have the `textobjects` installed for sane OOB captures. I can get the desired OOB experience by peppering the mini configs with the `use_nvim_treesitter` where required.

Yes, using `use_nvim_treesitter = true` is fine, but that only work for `master` branch of both 'nvim-treesitter' and 'nvim-treesitter-textobjects'. Because the `main` branch of 'nvim-treesitter' doesn't have necessary functionality.

I did/do have plans for completely removing `use_nvim_treesitter` option, but that will happen only after 'nvim-treesitter' has fully transitioned to `main` as default branch.

title: 'mini.surround' treesitter surrounding throws error with "@parameter" capture
